page: Microsoft Azure M64 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA instructions. The server is equipped with 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Additionally, it includes 7340 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as shown by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores. Memory performance is a notable strength; while small-block cached read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read bandwidth is strong, placing in the top 25%. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput consistently register in the middle 50%. Large-model LLM text generation is poor, though prompt processing speeds remain average for small and medium models.

Given its massive 1 TB memory capacity and bundled 7.3 TB local SSD, the M64 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. The qualitative cost efficiency is centered on its specialized memory-to-vCPU ratio rather than raw single-core compute power. This makes it highly suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and data-intensive ETL pipelines that require a substantial memory footprint and local scratch space but do not demand ultra-high single-threaded CPU speeds.
description: Microsoft Azure M64 is a memory-optimized server featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 1024.0 GB of RAM (16.0 GB per core) and 7340 GB of local SSD storage. While single-core benchmarks for this virtual machine fall in the bottom 10%, its multi-core performance and database operations align with the middle 50% of tested systems. Notably, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is strong, ranking in the top 25%. The server's high memory density and substantial local storage make it a solid choice for memory-intensive workloads, such as large databases, in-memory caching, and data-heavy enterprise applications, where memory capacity is prioritized over single-threaded compute speed.
